26.0.0.en: In this chapter He summarizes the divine commands mentioned in the Book of Leviticus. In this verse He forbids them the worship of idols, among which they lived in Egypt and which would surround them in the land of Canaan, and He gives details of the idols or images, which are:

26.0.1.en: 1- Making statues that they carve from any material in order to worship them.

26.0.2.en: 2- Setting up pillars, which are walls or columns that remind them of the pagan gods so that they may worship them.

26.0.3.en: 3- Stones carved in the form of the pagan gods.

26.0.4.en: What is meant is the prohibition of any form of idol worship, and rather the worship of the one God, the Creator of heaven and earth, as the second commandment stated (Ex 20:2, 3).

26.1.0.en: Here He calls them to two positive things in His worship, which are:

26.1.1.en: 1- Setting apart the Sabbath day for the worship of God, as the fourth commandment stated (Ex 20:8-11). This also includes the sanctification of the seventh year and the year of jubilee (ch. 25:1-22). The sanctification of the Sabbath distinguishes them from the rest of the peoples and gives them God's blessing on the remaining days of the week.

26.1.2.en: 2- Respect for the house of the Lord and offering sacrifices and prayers in it, because it is God's dwelling among them, so they enjoy His care and protection.

26.2.0.en: God sets a condition for receiving His blessings: not only knowing His commandments but applying them and acting by them. This shows God's concern for man's freedom and his obedience to His commandments, for they are the entrance to all the blessings, the most important of which He mentions in the following verses.

26.3.0.en: The first blessing is the coming down of rain from heaven at the times when the crops need it. This is essential in the cultivation of the land of Canaan, which depends on rain in addition to rivers. By this they obtain the produce of the field and the fruit of the trees, that is, they find their food. The rain is a symbol of the blessings of the Holy Spirit coming down to us from heaven, which we receive in the Church.

26.4.0.en: The second blessing is the abundance of the crops. Because of the abundance of the winter crops such as wheat and barley, the threshing of their grain, that is, separating the grain from the straw, continues from April to June, and so it joins with the time of the vintage, that is, the gathering of the fruits of the trees such as grapes and olives, which begins in June and continues until September, and this too joins with the time of winter sowing, which begins in the month of October. Thus the crops are abundant, so they are satisfied and thank God for His generosity.

26.4.1.en: He also promises them security as regards being satisfied with food and likewise protection from enemies, which He mentions in detail in the following verse.

26.5.0.en: The third blessing is peace and security, which is expressed by their sleeping a quiet sleep without any disturbance from two things, which are:

26.5.1.en: 1- Enemies, in that He puts the awe of His people in their hearts, so they do not think of attacking them or seizing their crops and their spoils.

26.5.2.en: 2- The wild beasts that were numerous in the land of Canaan, for He destroys them and drives them away from them.

26.5.3.en: If you obey God's commandments and are occupied with His love, trust that He supplies your needs and gives you the enjoyment of inner peace and gives you awe in the eyes of those around you, so that you remain in the enjoyment of fellowship with Him. So seek first the Kingdom of God and His righteousness, and know that the rest will be added to you.

26.6.0.en: The fourth blessing is strength and victory over enemies, if any of them dares and tries to attack them. They will conquer them, and they will flee before them, and they will drive them far from their land. There have been many examples of this, such as the victory of Moses over the Amalekites and of Joshua over the Canaanites.

26.7.1.en: The power of God is manifested with His children, so that a small number of them can conquer a great number of enemies. He gives examples, namely the victory of five of the people of God over a hundred of the enemies and of a hundred of the people of God over ten thousand of the enemies. This happened often, such as the victory of three hundred men with Gideon over thousands of Midianites, the victory of Samson alone over great numbers of the Philistines, and the victory of Judas Maccabeus with a small number over the armies of the Greek empire.

26.8.0.en: The fifth blessing is the multiplication of offspring, which gives strength to the people of God. By this He fulfills His promise and His covenant with the fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and this means His care for them, which preserves them and multiplies them.

26.9.2.en: God blesses their harvests that they gather, so that they are very abundant, so much so that they eat from the crop of the past year until the crop of the new year comes, and much of the old crops may remain with them for several years, and when the new crops are gathered they are compelled to empty the storehouses of the old crops, as it says, "ye shall bring forth the old because of the new," in order to put in the new, that is, the goodness and the satisfaction are in great abundance.

26.10.0.en: The sixth blessing is God's good pleasure in them, as proved by His dwelling in their midst in the tabernacle of meeting or the temple of Solomon. When they disobeyed God, He refused to dwell in their midst, as happened at the end of the life of Eli the priest, when the Ark of the Covenant went to the Philistines, and as happened during the Babylonian captivity, when they destroyed the temple of God and Jerusalem.

26.11.0.en: Since God is pleased with them, He accompanies them in all their journeys and cares for them, and His name is called upon them, and they are a people special to Him and are distinguished by this from the rest of the peoples.

26.12.0.en: The bands of your yoke: The yoke is a crosswise piece of wood placed on the necks of two animals and tied to each neck by a rope called a band, and what is meant by breaking the bands of the yoke is freedom from slavery. And made you go upright: that is, erect, with the head held high in dignity, instead of the stooping of humiliation and bondage in Egypt, and what is meant is the dignity and exaltation that belong to the free.

26.12.1.en: God reminds them of His freeing them from the bondage of Egypt and their victory over it, and that therefore He is able to make them always victorious over their enemies in every place if they keep His commandments.

26.13.0.en: Break: You break the covenant and the compact.

26.13.1.en: On the other hand, God makes clear the punishments and curses that come upon His people if they refuse to keep His commandments and walk by them, and hate them, and break the covenant with Him of living as a people special to Him. He makes clear these disciplines in the following verses.

26.14.0.en: The first discipline is terror and disease. Instead of inner peace, fear fills their hearts, and diseases spread among them, such as tuberculosis and fevers of various kinds. These diseases affect the different members of the body, the most important of which are the eyes, which grow weak until a person loses his sight, and they also affect their souls and not only their bodies, so they suffer from many troubles and psychological disturbances. The second discipline is the plundering of their goods by the enemies. After they labor in sowing their crops, the enemies attack at the time of harvest or gathering and take their produce, so the people of God become poor and hungry.

26.15.0.en: The third discipline is defeat before the enemies. For if they disobey God and defy Him, God becomes an adversary to them, so they are defeated before their enemies however weak the latter are, and out of their fear they flee from the enemies even if the enemies do not pursue them, because terror fills their hearts, since God has forsaken them and has even become against them because of their sins, by which they rejected God.

26.15.1.en: Do not reject God and persist in sin and be careless about it, then afterward return to murmur because God has forsaken you. Know that the one who began the wrong is you and not God, so review yourself, and do not lose the most precious thing, which is the Kingdom, for the sake of trifling matters, which are the pleasures of this passing world and its evil desires.

26.16.0.en: If they accept the discipline and return to God in repentance, He forgives them, but if they persist in their sins, God increases the disciplines upon them sevenfold, that is, the fullness of discipline, until they repent and return.

26.17.0.en: The fourth discipline is humiliation. He removes from them their pride and dignity, which He gave them when He brought them out of the land of Egypt and by His care for them in the wilderness and when He gave them the land of Canaan to possess. So the enemies rise against them to occupy them and humble them.

26.17.1.en: The fifth discipline is the standing of nature against them, so that the heaven becomes like iron, that is, it gives them no rain, so cultivation fails and they suffer from hunger, and likewise the earth becomes like brass, that is, it loses its fertility and its ability to make the crops grow, so they are also exposed to hunger.

26.18.0.en: He explains and completes what He said in the previous verse concerning their loss of the produce of the land because of nature's defiance of them. However much they labor in cultivating the land, they reap nothing because of the land's defiance of them or because of pests, so they neither reap nor gather anything of the crops or the fruit of the trees, or they take very little, spoiled, which does not suffice them.

26.19.0.en: Here He repeats that if they do not submit to the divine discipline and repent of their sins, God will increase upon them the discipline and the blessings, perhaps they will take heed and repent.

26.20.0.en: The sixth discipline is the attack of wild beasts upon them, so that they devour their children and their cattle, and their number decreases and their strength weakens. This actually happened when the serpents bit the people in the days of Moses (Num 21:5, 6) and when two she bears devoured forty and two of the children who mocked Elisha (2 Kgs 2:23, 24).

26.21.0.en: Here He affirms to His people for a third time that if they persist in their sins, He will continue to discipline them and even multiply it sevenfold, that is, the fullness of discipline, so that they may submit and return from their sins.

26.22.0.en: Here He affirms their defeat before the enemies, who strike them with the sword and kill them, in addition to the spread of plagues with various diseases that finish them. By this God breaks His covenant with them of blessing and protection, because they transgressed His commandments, so He forsook them and the enemies and the plagues attacked them.

26.23.0.en: The seventh discipline is the famine, which has been referred to and which resulted from the previous disciplines.

26.23.1.en: Because bread is the basis of food, He calls it the staff of bread, since a person leans and relies on a staff, so God breaks the staff of bread, that is, a famine occurs. He expresses the details of this famine by saying that the oven, that is, the furnace that would suffice for the baking of one woman or one house, will, because of the scarcity of the crops and the lack of flour except a little in every house, suffice for the baking of ten houses or ten women. He affirms the famine by saying that the bread will be given to people by weight because of its scarcity, so they return it, that is, they turn it over in their hands with care, and weigh a small amount for each person, so that he does not eat more than it because of hunger.

26.24.0.en: Here God repeats to His people that if they disobey Him and transgress His commandments, He will forsake them and will also walk with them in fierce wrath, so He permits disciplines sevenfold upon them because of their defiance and rebellion, perhaps they will repent.

26.25.0.en: From the severity of the hunger that God permits, a person loses his natural feelings and becomes like a ravening beast, so he slaughters his sons and eats them in order to live. This actually happened in the siege of Jerusalem by Babylon (Lam 4:9, 10) and in the siege of Jerusalem by the Romans in AD 70.

26.26.0.en: The eighth discipline is the destruction of the altars of the idols that were set up on the hills and the images of the sun that they hung on wooden columns, which are the posts, or placed in houses for the worship of the sun. God also permits them to be killed by the sword and their corpses to be cast upon the carcasses of the animals that they offered on the altars of the idols, that is, they die in their evil by forsaking God and worshiping foreign gods.

26.27.0.en: God continues His discipline by destroying the cities and likewise the holy places, which are His temple in Jerusalem, as happened during the attack of Babylon and its destruction of the temple and Jerusalem, and as also happened when the Romans destroyed the temple. God adds that He will not accept their sacrifices that they offer to Him, that is, He rejects their worship because of their persistence in evil.

26.28.0.en: As a continuation of the blow of destruction, the land becomes desolate, that is, ruined, and wild beasts dwell in it, so that their enemies who occupy them cannot bear to live in their desolate lands and are amazed at this ruin to which the cities of the people of God have come.

26.29.0.en: I will draw out a sword: I will take it out of its sheath to kill many with it, and what is meant is that He permits the enemies, whom God regards as His sword, to kill them.

26.29.1.en: As an extension of the ruin of their cities, they are scattered in the countries of the world, where the enemies carry them off after killing many of them, and so their lands and their cities remain ruined.

26.30.0.en: Her sabbaths: What is meant by the sabbath is the seventh year, in which the commandment ordered that the land not be cultivated.

26.30.1.en: The people of God neglected for a long time to carry out His commandments by not cultivating the land in the seventh year and in the year of jubilee, that is, the fiftieth year. So God permitted the land to be ruined and not cultivated, in place of the seventh year in which they ought not to have sown, and the captivity lasts long enough, and the land lies ruined without cultivation, until the years in which they ought not to have cultivated it are fulfilled, but they transgressed God's commandments and cultivated it.

26.30.2.en: By this they lost the blessing of God that He used to give them in the sixth year, then their lands were ruined for many years and their cities too were destroyed, and they came under the divine wrath.

26.31.1.en: Here He affirms the first discipline, which is the casting of fear into the hearts of the people of God while they are captives. They fear though no one frightens them, so that even the movement of a leaf of a tree in the wind disturbs their hearts and they flee though their enemies do not pursue them, because fear has filled their hearts.

26.32.0.en: He continues the discipline of fear that comes upon them. They flee though no one chases them, because of the intensity of their anxiety, and as they flee one stumbles upon another and they fall to the ground as they run. Thus they continue in their defeat before the enemies though the enemies have left them, but fear continues to disturb them and drives them.

26.33.0.en: Thus the people of God grow weak and many of them perish in the land of the enemies, and they lose their lineages, their nationality and their worship, and so become worthless.

26.34.0.en: The remaining captives of the people of God perish in the lands of the enemies because of their sins and the sins of their fathers in which they continued, whether by the worship of idols or by the many unclean lusts.

26.35.0.en: Their uncircumcised hearts: that is, those not circumcised, and what is meant is not believing and renewed by faith to live in purity with God.

26.35.1.en: After showing His blessings for those who obey His commandments and His disciplines for those who transgress them, He gives hope to those who transgressed against Him and understood and accepted His disciplines, so they repented and returned to Him, and He embraces them with His mercies. This repentance means confessing their sins and the sins of their fathers in which they continued. By this they transgressed against God, so God walked contrary to them, that is, He forsook them and permitted their discipline and their scattering in the countries of their enemies, who carried them away from their land. By this confession they declare the return of their hearts to faith and their acceptance of the discipline they deserve because of their disobedience.

26.36.0.en: I will remember My covenant: This does not mean that God had forgotten, but a divine declaration that He will fulfill His covenant and His promise.

26.36.1.en: The mercies of God to His repentant children appear in that He fulfills to them His promises of caring for them and protecting them, as He promised their father Jacob, the father of the tribes, and their forefathers Isaac and Abraham (Gen 22:16-18), (Gen 26:1-6), (Gen 35:9-15). And He brings them back to the Promised Land after their captivity.

26.37.0.en: Enjoy her sabbaths: Explained before in (v. 35), that is, it is not cultivated, in place of the seventh year in which they did not sanctify the land to God by not cultivating it.

26.37.1.en: Desolate: The land remains desolate, that is, uncultivated.

26.37.2.en: They despised My judgments: They disobeyed and refused to obey My judgments.

26.37.3.en: God has mercy on His repentant children after He disciplined them by moving them from their lands at the hands of the enemies. They left the land uncultivated as a result of their transgression in former times and their disobedience to the commandment of the seventh year, in which He commanded them not to cultivate the land. So as a punishment they leave their land against their will, uncultivated and desolate for long years.

26.38.0.en: I have not abhorred them: I have not forsaken them and withheld My fatherhood from them.

26.38.1.en: To break My covenant: To violate My covenant.

26.38.2.en: The mercies of God also appear in His not hating His people when they disobeyed Him. He scattered them in the countries of the enemies but did not destroy them, and He kept waiting until they repented, so that He would fulfill His covenant and His fatherhood and care for them and bring them back to their land in glory and honor.

26.38.3.en: God's tenderness toward you continues even while you are in sin, and He awaits your return to embrace you with His mercies. You will not find tenderness like His in the world, so do not delay repentance and returning to Him.

26.39.0.en: God affirms that He will fulfill His promises to the first fathers, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and so He will have mercy on His repentant people whom He brought out of the land of Egypt and will restore His care and protection to them.

26.40.0.en: Here God concludes His speech, saying that what has gone before are God's laws for His children, that they may live by them.

26.40.1.en: Vows, firstborn, devoted things and tithes (1) Vows:

26.40.2.en: A – Of persons (vv. 1-8) 1 And the LORD spake unto Moses, saying, 2 "Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, When a man shall make a singular vow, the persons shall be for the LORD by thy estimation. 3 And thy estimation shall be of the male from twenty years old even unto sixty years old, even thy estimation shall be fifty shekels of silver, after the shekel of the sanctuary. 4 And if it be a female, then thy estimation shall be thirty shekels. 5 And if it be from five years old even unto twenty years old, then thy estimation shall be of the male twenty shekels, and for the female ten shekels. 6 And if it be from a month old even unto five years old, then thy estimation shall be of the male five shekels of silver, and for the female thy estimation shall be three shekels of silver. 7 And if it be from sixty years old and above; if it be a male, then thy estimation shall be fifteen shekels, and for the female ten shekels. 8 But if he be poorer than thy estimation, then he shall present himself before the priest, and the priest shall value him; according to his ability that vowed shall the priest value him."
